question.problem: The $7$th and $8$th terms of an arithmetic sequence are $-39$ and $-31,$ respectively. Determine the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

Since the terms ${a}_{7}=-39$ and ${a}_{8}=-31$ are consecutive, we can subtract them to find the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{8}-{a}_{7} \\  & =-31-(-39) \\  & =-31+39 \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{7}=-39,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{7}$ is $6$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{7} & ={a}_{1}+6d \\ -39 & ={a}_{1}+6(8) \\ -39 & ={a}_{1}+48 \\ -39-48 & ={a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =-87.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-87+(n-1)(8) \\  & =-87+8n-8 \\  & =8n-95.\end{aligned}
$$
